room_name: Le salon des voyages · The travel lounge
hook: "zhah-poh-NEH": a girl opens her bento lunch box beside the red-sun flag of JAPAN: zhah-poh-NEH ≈ JAPAN-AY
note: Japanese; le japonais = the Japanese language; un Japonais, une Japonaise = a Japanese person (capitalized).

room_name: Le salon des voyages · The travel lounge
hook: "an-DYAN": a woman pours tea next to the saffron, white and green flag of India: IN-DYAN: an-DYAN ≈ INDIAN
note: Indian (from India). Also the dated word for Native Americans (les Indiens d'Amérique), now usually les Amérindiens or les Autochtones.

room_name: Le salon des voyages · The travel lounge
hook: "BAHSK": a boy BASKS in a warm sunbeam holding a pelota ball and the curved wicker glove of the Basque ball game: BASK: BAHSK ≈ BASK
note: Basque (from the Basque Country, le Pays basque); le basque = the Basque language; un béret basque = a beret.

room_name: Le salon des voyages · The travel lounge
hook: "bruh-TOHN": BRET hauls a TON of crêpes past the black-and-white flag of Brittany: BRET-TON: bruh-TOHN ≈ BRET-TON
note: From Brittany (la Bretagne); le breton = the Breton language. Not British (= britannique).

room_name: Le salon des voyages · The travel lounge
hook: "proh-vahn-SAHL": a toy VAN loaded with lavender from PROVENCE: PRO-VAN-SAL: proh-vahn-SAHL ≈ PRO-VAN-SAL
note: From Provence; les herbes de Provence = Provence herbs. Feminine provençale, masculine plural provençaux.

room_name: Le salon des voyages · The travel lounge
hook: "MOHV": a girl in a mauve dress sways and MOVES to the music: MOHV ≈ MOVE
note: Mauve, pale purple; usually agrees in the plural (des robes mauves). Also la mauve = the mallow plant.

room_name: La véranda · The glass veranda
hook: "ah-doh-lay-SAHNS": a teenage girl on the swing, headphones on, rolls her eyes: ADOLESCENCE: ah-doh-leh-SAHNSS ≈ ADOLESCENCE
note: Adolescence, the teenage years; a teenager is un or une adolescent(e), or ado for short.

room_name: La véranda · The glass veranda
hook: "GOS": a little kid plays GHOST under a white bedsheet: GHOS(T): GOHSS ≈ GHOS(T)
note: Kid (familiar, un or une gosse). In Quebec French les gosses is vulgar slang, so say enfant there.

room_name: La véranda · The glass veranda
hook: "ruh-koh-neh-SAHN": the girl RECOGNIZES her lost raccoon and is so grateful: RECOGNIZING: ruh-koh-neh-SAHN ≈ RECOGNIZ(ING)
note: Grateful (reconnaissant envers quelqu'un); from reconnaître = to recognize. Je vous suis reconnaissant = I am grateful to you.

room_name: La véranda · The glass veranda
hook: "ahn-nwee-YEUH": a dull slideshow of brown dots ANNOYS this yawning boy: ANNOY-YUH: ahn-nwee-YEUH ≈ ANNOY-YUH
note: Boring, and also annoying or awkward (c'est ennuyeux = that's a nuisance).

room_name: La véranda · The glass veranda
hook: "ah-bee-TWEHL": grandpa sinks into his usual chair out of HABIT, WELL settled: HABIT-WELL: ah-bee-TWEHL ≈ HABIT-WELL
note: Usual, habitual; comme d'habitude = as usual.

room_name: La véranda · The glass veranda
hook: "vee-VAHN": a jolly BON VIVANT tucks into a huge slice of cream cake: vee-VAHN ≈ (bon) VIVANT
note: Un vivant = a living person (les vivants et les morts); un bon vivant = someone who enjoys life. As an adjective: alive, lively.

room_name: La véranda · The glass veranda
hook: "byan-vuh-NEW": a host in a BEE-striped sweater flings the garden door open AND welcomes everyone to his VENUE: BEE-AN-VENUE: byan-vuh-NU ≈ BEE-AN-VENUE
note: Le bienvenu, la bienvenue = the welcome guest (soyez le bienvenu). Bienvenue! = Welcome!

room_name: La véranda · The glass veranda
hook: "MAHL": the male peacock struts his tail like a model at the MALL: MAHL ≈ MALL
note: Un mâle = a male (animal); as an adjective male, also manly. The female is la femelle.

room_name: Le salon de thé · The tea room
hook: "zhay-nay-REUH": a man squirts a GENEROUS mountain of whipped cream on a girl's cocoa: GENER-UH(S): zhay-nay-REUH ≈ GENER(OUS)
note: Generous; also ample or full-bodied (un vin généreux).

room_name: Le salon de thé · The tea room
hook: "rehs-pehk-TAHBL": a dignified lady in pearls sips her tea, little finger raised: RESPECT-ABLE: reh-spehk-TAHBL ≈ RESPECT-ABLE
note: Respectable; also sizeable (une somme respectable = a tidy sum).

room_name: Le salon de thé · The tea room
hook: "ay-kee-TAHBL": a girl rules the cake into perfectly EQUAL slices on the TABLE: EQUI-TABLE: ay-kee-TAHBL ≈ EQUI-TABLE
note: Fair, even-handed; le commerce équitable = fair trade.

room_name: Le salon de thé · The tea room
hook: "oh-blee-ZHAY": a boy is forced to share his scone with a cheeky bird: OH, BLUE JAY!: oh-blee-ZHAY ≈ OH, BLUE JAY
note: Obliged, forced (être obligé de = to have to); in formal style also grateful (je vous suis obligé).

room_name: Le salon de thé · The tea room
hook: "fah-voh-RAHBL": a man taps the barometer and the needle swings to the sun: FAVOR-ABLE weather: fah-voh-RAHBL ≈ FAVOR-ABLE
note: Favourable; être favorable à = to be in favour of.

room_name: Le salon de thé · The tea room
hook: "proh-feh-syoh-NEHL": a waitress balances ten teacups on one hand like a true PROFESSIONAL: proh-feh-syoh-NEHL ≈ PROFESSIONAL
note: Professional; also vocational (le lycée professionnel). Un or une professionnel(le) = a pro.

room_name: La garde-robe · The dressing room
hook: "ee-dahn-TEEK": twin girls in exactly matching dresses: EE-DAHN-TEEK, IDENTI-CAL: ee-dahn-TEEK ≈ IDENTI(CAL)
note: Identical, the same (identique à = identical to).

room_name: La garde-robe · The dressing room
hook: "pahr-SYEHL": a jacket with only ONE sleeve sewn on: only PARTIAL: par-SYEL ≈ PARTIAL
note: Partial, in part (une vue partielle). False friend: French partial means biased. Un partiel = a university exam.

room_name: La garde-robe · The dressing room
hook: "goor-MAHN": a boy with an éclair in each hand and cream on his nose, a little GOURMET MAN: GOOR-MAHN: goor-MAHN ≈ GOOR-MAN (gourmet man)
note: Fond of food, sweet-toothed; milder than 'glutton' (that's glouton). Un gourmand = a foodie.

room_name: La garde-robe · The dressing room
hook: "MOSH": a boy in a lumpy, clashing snowman sweater so ugly the others want to MOSH it away: MOSH: MOSH ≈ MOSH
note: Ugly (informal); also rotten, a shame (c'est moche = that's too bad). Rude about a person.

room_name: La garde-robe · The dressing room
hook: "gloh-RYEUH": a girl in a golden cape and medal raises her arms in GLORY on the stool: GLOR-YEUH: glor-YEUH ≈ GLORY-UH
note: Glorious; in older style also vain or boastful about one's glory.

room_name: La garde-robe · The dressing room
hook: "MEHGR": a skinny greyhound in a little coat bares its teeth: MAY GRR!: MEH-gruh ≈ MAY GRR
note: Thin, skinny (can be unkind about a person); also low-fat (fromage maigre) and meagre (un maigre salaire).
